proposals.relationship: Judt names Hobsbawm as a major model for clear, large-scale narrative and analytical history accessible to a general audience.
proposals.evidence_note: Own Q15 explicitly answers who most influenced his work and immediately retains political disagreement. This positive writing/model testimony differs from existing1137 critique of the categories and coverage of The Age of Extremes; neither arrow cancels the other. No particular Hobsbawm edition or universal political agreement inferred.
primary_locators: Yerxa interview2005/published2006,Q15 “Who has influenced your work the most?”

proposals.relationship: Judt uses Marx’s distinction between making history and inherited constraints to explain individual agency in postwar Europe.
proposals.evidence_note: Own Q9 explicitly attributes the formulation to Marx and develops it through postwar constraints and contingent political action, including de Gaulle, Thatcher and the breakup of Yugoslavia/Czechoslovakia. Bounded conceptual resource, not general Marxist allegiance, automatic teacher lineage or proof of reading a particular Marx original/edition.
primary_locators: Yerxa interview2005/published2006,Q9 agency and forces unleashed by war

proposals.relationship: Judt endorses and supports Furet’s argument linking the inherited myth of the French Revolution with Western credit accorded the Russian Revolution.
proposals.evidence_note: Own1997 P25–28 distinguishes prior communist-myth scholarship from Furet’s synthesis and explicitly defends the French/Russian linkage against exaggeration criticism with a1936 Ligue report example. This is a particular argumentative uptake, not membership in a formal school: n7/P55 calls newspaper school membership flattering but misleading; P31 qualifies the unity of Furet’s oeuvre. Riley2011:35–40 separately criticizes Judt’s Furet-related changes, not independently certified by this resource claim. Le Passé d’une illusion1995 unread.

proposals.relationship: Judt criticizes Thompson’s prolixity and political provincialism while praising the empathetic history and historical examples in several of his books.
proposals.evidence_note: Own reply2007:P22–24 praises Making, Whigs and Hunters and anti-Althusser historical common sense, then faults lengths and uses Thompson’s response to a Czech dissident as an example of parochial East/West equivalence. Countryman’s preceding letter challenges Judt’s tone, caricature and attribution of system-building, and defends enduring scholarship. The1981 exchange is known here through Judt, not independently checked; no dismissal of all Thompson history or proof of domestic insider knowledge.

proposals.relationship: Cohen credits Judt’s call to reconnect social history with politics as part of the challenge that shaped Making a New Deal’s research question.
proposals.evidence_note: Own recipient retrospective2008preface:xxi–xxii/n2 cites Judt1979 alongside joint Evans/Rueschemeyer/Skocpol1985volume. Cohen explicitly takes this challenge toward politically inflected social history while preserving everyday social/cultural experience, not wholesale acceptance of polemical rhetoric. Dissertation1982–86/book1990 and retrospective second edition2008 separated. Original Judt essay and joint state volume unread; parent reserved this pair to Judt dossier.
